data.description: Early to Late Triassic unit in New Jersey, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Virginia; aka Newark Supergroup, Newark Group

Early Triassic (locally Middle Triassic) unit in Arizona, California, Colorado, New Mexico, Nevada, Utah. Some publications (see Lucas et al. 2007) recognize it as group status in Utah, Colorado, and Wyoming.
Supergroup in Antarctica spanning the Early Devonian to the Early Triassic
A Middle Triassic, Anisian unit in western Europe, limestone; sometimes referred to as a formation.
pending
Late Cretaceous (Santonian) unit in Mississippi; referred to as both formation and group
A Cretaceous unit in Germany.

Early to Middle Mississippian (Tournaisian to Visean; Kinderhookian to Meramecian) unit in Indiana, Kentucky, Illinois; referred to as formation in Indiana, Kentucky, Ohio, Tennessee, and West Virginia; aka Borden Siltstone
Oligocene unit in New Mexico and Arizona, aka Datil Formation, Datil Volcanics
Middle Pennsylvanian to Early Permian unit in Arizona and New Mexico; aka Naco Formation and Naco Limestone
Early to early Late Cretaceous (Aptian to Cenomanian) unit in Virginia, Washington D.C., Maryland, Delaware, and New Jersey; referred to as formation and group
Devonian unit in Alabama; aka Talladega Slate, Talladega Formation, Talladega Group
Mississippian (Osagean to Chesterian) unit in New Mexico, formerly referred to as Arroyo Penasco Formation
Late Triassic unit in New Mexico and Texas; aka Chinle Formation of Dockum Group, rocks of this name may extend to Colorado, Arizona, Nevada, and Utah as well

Middle to Late Pennsylvanian (Desmoinesian to Virgilian) unit in Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia; aka Conemaugh Formation in Illinois, Kentucky, Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia

early Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) and locally late Early Cretaceous (Albian) unit in Colorado, Kansas, Nebraska, New Mexico, and North Dakota; aka Dakota Sandstone, Dakota Formation, Dakota Conglomerate

Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian to Turonian) unit in Texas, Oklahoma, and Louisiana; Named from exposures at Eagle Ford, Dallas Co., northeastern TX (Hill, 1887); aka Eagle Ford Shale, Eagle Ford Clay, Eagle Ford Formation of Tuscaloosa Group
Late Cambrian (Croixan) to Early Ordovician (Canadian) unit in Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas; aka El Paso Limestone, El Paso Dolomite, El Paso Formation
Middle Ordovician, Late Ordovician (Mohawkian to Cincinnatian) unit in Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, and Wisconsin; aka Galena Dolomite, Galena Formation, may be part of Sinnipee Group
Middle Devonian unit in Marlyand, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and West Virginia; aka Hamilton Shale, Hamilton Formation, and Hamilton Shale Member of Romney Formation
Late Ordovician (Cincinnatian) unit in New Mexico and Texas; aka Montoya Dolomite, may be referred to as Montoya Formation
Late Cretaceous unit in Washington; aka Nanaimo Formation

Early to Middle Pennsylvanian (Namurian to Westphalian; Morrowan to Atokan) unit in New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia; may also be referred to as formation in Alabama, Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia

late Early to early Late Cretaceous (Albian to Cenomanian) unit in Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Utah, and Wyoming; aka Colorado Shale or Colorado Formation, but these names not used by the Colorado Geological Survey
middle Permian to Early Triassic unit in South Africa
Cretaceous unit in Patagonia
Silurian unit in Ireland, includes Ferriters Cove Formation, Drom Point Formation, Clogher Head Formation, Croaghmahrin Formation

Cretaceous to Eocene unit in the European Alps; described in: Stern, Gerald, and Michael Wagreich. "Provenance of the Upper Cretaceous to Eocene Gosau Group around and beneath the Vienna Basin (Austria and Slovakia)." Swiss Journal of Geosciences 106 (2013): 505-527
Pleistocene unit in central Japanese island chain, deposited in the Kanto Tectonic Basin in response to the west-northwestward subduction of the Pacific plate beneath the Philippine Sea Plate
Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) unit in the Kem Kem region of eastern Morocco
Plio-Pleistocene unit in Japan
late Permian and/or Early Triassic unit of the Beaufort Group in South Africa
Albian to Neocomian (Cretaceous) unit in west Africa

late Miocene to early Pleistocene unit in Costa Rica

Santonian to Campanian unit in Canada

Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous unit in Arizona
middle Eocene unit in England, formerly Bracklesham Beds
Barremian to early Albian unit in Alberta, British Columbia

Late Triassic (Early Carnian to Early Norian) unit in North Carolina and South Carolina, part of Newark Supergroup

early Late Devonian (Frasnian) unit in New York and West Virginia
late Oligocene to late Pliocene unit in Delaware, Washington D.C., Maryland, North Carolina, and Virginia
Chesterian unit of central North America (Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, Colorado)
middle to late Paleozoic unit in Washington
Late Ordovician unit of Ohio

early Tertiary (early to middle Eocene) unit in southeastern North America

late Carboniferous to early Permian unit in South Africa

Late Cretaceous unit in Alberta, Canada; Lithology: Predominantly of fresh to brackish water, fine-grained sandstone, calcareous sandstones, sandy shales, bentonitic sandstones and shales, bentonite, ironstone nodules, concretions and bands, carbonaceous shales and coal. Hard, flaggy sandstones commonly cap mesas, buttes and plateaus where erosion of the formation results in 'badland' topography
Early Cretaceous unit in Arkansas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas, and Louisiana
Late Pennsylvanian (Virgilian) unit in New Mexico; controversially referred to as "group" as there is only one subunit (Bruton Formation) and groups consist of two or more formations
Miocene to Pliocene(?) unit in Arizona and New Mexico, aka Gila Conglomerate

Bajocian-Callovian unit in England
Mesoproterozoic (Middle Proterozoic) unit in New York; aka Grenville Complex

late Oligocene to late Miocene unit in Colombia

Jurassic unit in Europe
Paleogene to Neogene unit in Arkansas and North Carolina

Eocene unit in British Columbia, Canada; Lithology: The Kamloops Group forms an extensive succession of basalt, andesite, and subordinate felsic rocks with a calc-alkaline (subduction-related) geochemical signature

Late Pennsylvanian (Virgilian) unit in New Mexico; no current usage, rocks of Keller Group reallocated to Atrasado Formation of Madera Group
Cenozoic unit in Alaska

Permian (Roadian) to Triassic (Ladinian) unit in Germany; Predominantly pebbles and dolomitic clay pebbles, multicolored (reddish brown, violet, green, yellowish and others) with gray sections, in stratigraphic and regionally changing perimeters inclusions of dolomitic limestone (or limestone), anhydrite (or secondary gypsum or leaching residuals), rock salt, sandstone, conglomerate
Precambrian (middle to late Proterozoic) unit in Michigan, Wisconsin, and Minnesota

Late Pennsylvannian to Permian (Morrowan to Guadalupian) unit in Alaska

Permian unit in Orogrande basin, San Juan basin, Estancia basin; no current usage, Manzano Group (NM) replaced with (ascending): Bursum Formation, Abo Formation, Yeso Formation, Glorieta Sandstone, and San Andres Limestone. See Bursum, Abo, Yeso, Glorieta, and San Andres.

Jurassic (Pliensbachian - Bathonian) unit in Queensland, Australia; Fine to coarse-grained, thin- to very thick- bedded, crossbedded, quartzose to lithofeldspathic sandstone, interbedded with polymictic pebble and minor cobble conglomerate, siltstone and claystone; minor coal and basalt, fossil wood ferruginous oolite; Formerly referred to as the Marburg sequence ('formation', 'sandstone')
